This page provides a quick introduction to using `eotools` for atmospheric correction of satellite imagery.

## Installation

Install directly from [Hygeos GitHub](https://github.com/hygeos/eotools):

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/hygeos/eotools.git
```

This installs the required dependencies, including [`hygeos-core`](https://pypi.org/project/hygeos-core/) (common utilities, imported as `hygeos_core`) and [`luts`](https://pypi.org/project/luts/).

The level-1 readers and ancillary data providers come from [`eoread`](https://pypi.org/project/eoread/) (version 2 or later), an optional dependency installed with the `eoread` extra:

```bash
pip install "eotools[eoread] @ git+https://github.com/hygeos/eotools.git"
```

`eotools` relies on auxiliary data (data files, meteo files, etc.) that are fetched automatically.

Data directories are managed by `hygeos_core.env`. Set the `DIR_DATA` environment variable to point to your data directory. Other paths (`static`, `ancillary`, `sample_products`) default to subdirectories under it.

```bash
export DIR_DATA="$HOME/eo_data"
```

You can also set it in a `.env` file in your working directory. If undefined, data defaults to `./data`.


## Quick example: Gaseous & Rayleigh correction

### From command line

Process a level1 product with the `eoread.readers.planetscope.Level1_PLANETSCOPE` reader, and write it to netcdf:

```bash
python -m eotools.rayleigh \
    /path/to/level1_product \
    eoread.readers.planetscope.Level1_PLANETSCOPE \
    /path/to/output.nc
```

Available readers include all sensors available in `eoread`:

- `eoread.readers.msi.Level1C_MSI`
- `eoread.readers.olci.Level1_OLCI`
- `eoread.readers.oli.Level1_OLI`
- `eoread.readers.planetscope.Level1_PLANETSCOPE`
- `eoread.readers.pleiades.Level1_PLEIADES`
- `eoread.readers.pleiades_neo.Level1_PNEO`
- `eoread.readers.geosat.Level1_GEOSAT`

### With `process_rayleigh`

For programmatic use, `process_rayleigh` handles file I/O and applies the full correction pipeline:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from eotools.rayleigh import process_rayleigh

process_rayleigh(
    input_product=Path("/path/to/level1_product"),
    reader="eoread.readers.planetscope.Level1_PLANETSCOPE",
    output_product=Path("/path/to/output.nc"),
    dem="eotools.dem.CopernicusDEM",
)
```

### With `process_rayleigh_dataset`

To work with an `xarray.Dataset` directly (e.g., for further custom processing), use `process_rayleigh_dataset`:

```python
from eoread.readers.planetscope import Level1_PLANETSCOPE
from eotools.rayleigh import process_rayleigh_dataset
from hygeos_core.files.save import to_netcdf

# Load a Level-1 dataset
ds = Level1_PLANETSCOPE("/path/to/level1_product")

# Apply the full Rayleigh correction pipeline
result = process_rayleigh_dataset(
    ds,
    dem="eotools.dem.GTOPO30",
    transmittance_corr=True,
)

# Access corrected reflectance
rho_rc = result["rho_rc"]

# Write the full corrected dataset to a NetCDF file
to_netcdf(result, filename="/path/to/output.nc")
```


## Output variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `rho_gc` | Gaseous-corrected reflectance |
| `rho_rc` | Rayleigh-corrected surface reflectance |
| `rho_r` | Rayleigh reflectance (without glint) |
| `rho_rg` | Rayleigh + sun glint reflectance |
| `t_d` | Total atmospheric transmittance |
| `odr` | Rayleigh optical depth |
